**Goal:** Have the wooden kayak (stitch‑and‑glue build) ready before the lake‑season opens (≈ early September).  
**Assumption:** You can work each weekend (Friday evening – Sunday afternoon) and have a garage/workshop that stays ≈ 15‑20 °C (good for epoxy [[concepts/epoxy‑curing‑management]]).  

Below is a **6‑week, weekend‑by‑weekend plan** that follows the recommended build order and epoxy‑curing best‑practice from the stitch‑and‑glue guidance [[summaries/session-05_2025-05-24]] and uses the proven time‑blocking pattern from the weekend‑routine example [[summaries/session-35_2025-07-24]].

| Week | Friday 6:30‑8 pm (prep) | Saturday (core build) | Sunday (finish / cure) | Key Deliverable |
|------|--------------------------|------------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| **1** (Aug 8‑9) | Lay out all pre‑cut plywood panels, check for damage, label each panel (bow, stern, side, deck). Clean surfaces. | **Panel fair‑and‑tack** – align panels, drill stitch‑holes, loosely tack with cheap “stitch‑and‑glue” wire. | Leave tack‑up to cure overnight; store panels flat under a tarp. | All panels are **fair‑ed, tacked, and ready for epoxy**. |
| **2** (Aug 15‑16) | Mix a small batch of epoxy (≈ 1 L) to test temperature & pot life; set up a clean work‑area. | **Epoxy fillet #1** – run continuous fillets along all interior seams (edges already tacked). Use **[[entities/epoxy‑resin]]** and keep humidity low. | Allow fillets to cure (≥ 4 h) then **light‑sand** the fillets to smooth. | First set of interior fillets cured and sanded. |
| **3** (Aug 22‑23) | Prep fiberglass cloth (cut to size) and clean cured fillets. | **Fiberglass lay‑up #1** – wet‑out cloth with epoxy, apply over interior fillets, roll out bubbles. | Cure overnight (keep garage temperature steady). | Interior is **glass‑reinforced**; structural strength increased. |
| **4** (Aug 29‑30) | Inspect interior glass; sand any high spots; clean dust. | **Second epoxy fillet pass** – add a thin “fill‑coat” fillet over the glass to seal any gaps. | Cure, then **wet‑sand** (220‑320 grit) to a smooth finish. | Seam‑sealing is **complete**; hull is watertight inside. |
| **5** (Sep 5‑6) | Cut and prep **exterior fiberglass** pieces (deck, sides). | **Exterior glass‑lay‑up** – apply epoxy‑wet cloth over the outside of the hull, overlapping deck edges. | Cure, then **sand** and **apply a final “fair‑coat”** of epoxy for a smooth surface. | Hull is fully **glass‑covered** on both sides. |
| **6** (Sep 12‑13) | Set up a clean, dust‑free area; gather finishing supplies (paint or marine varnish, sandpaper, polishing pads). | **Finish work** – sand to final smoothness, wipe clean, apply 2‑3 coats of marine‑grade paint/varnish (allow 24 h between coats). | Final cure; install **seat, foot‑rest, deck‑hardware** (pre‑drilled). | Kayak is **finished, sealed, and ready for launch** before the first weekend of September lake‑season. |

### How the schedule respects the key constraints

| Constraint | How it’s handled |
|------------|------------------|
| **Epoxy timing & temperature** – work when garage temperature is stable (early evening or mid‑morning) and humidity low [[concepts/epoxy‑curing‑management]] | All epoxy steps are placed on Saturday mornings (mid‑morning) or Friday evenings when temperature is predictable. |
| **Weekend‑routine flow** – short prep on Friday, focused build Saturday, cure & cleanup Sunday [[concepts/weekend‑routine]] | Each weekend follows the same block pattern used in the meal‑prep schedule (prep → main task → finish). |
| **Progressive curing** – never start a new epoxy layer until the previous one is fully cured and sanded | Each week ends with a “cure overnight” step, giving ample time for the resin to reach full strength. |
| **Tool & material readiness** – all panels, epoxy, fiberglass, sandpaper, and finishing supplies are staged the night before | Friday evening prep ensures Saturday starts with everything at hand, minimizing idle time. |
| **Safety & clean‑up** – keep a dedicated “wet‑area” for epoxy work, wear gloves, and have a water‑spray bottle for blush removal (quick wash) | The schedule includes a dedicated cleaning step after each epoxy cure (Saturday night or Sunday). |

### Quick reference checklist (copy‑paste for your planner)

```
Week 1 – Fair & tack panels
Week 2 – Interior epoxy fillets + sand
Week 3 – Interior fiberglass lay‑up
Week 4 – Second fillet pass + sand
Week 5 – Exterior fiberglass + final fillet
Week 6 – Sand → paint/varnish → hardware install
```

Follow this plan, keep the garage temperature around 15‑20 °C, and you’ll have a fully built, waterproof wooden kayak ready **before the first weekend of September** when the lake season opens. Happy building!
